map.🧪 色盲模拟器 Pro：8 型模拟 · 图片 · WCAG · 安全配色: 🧪 Color Blindness Simulator Pro: 8 Types · Image · WCAG · Safe Palette
map.专业色觉缺陷（CVD）模拟器。支持红色盲、红色弱、绿色盲、绿色弱、蓝色盲、蓝色弱: Professional color-vision-deficiency (CVD) simulator. Supports real-time simulation of 8 types—protanopia, protanomaly, deuteranopia, deuteranomaly, tritanopia, tritanomaly, achromatopsia, and blue-cone monochromacy—applied to a single color, a whole palette, or an uploaded image; built-in WCAG 2.1 contrast check, CIE ΔE color-difference matrix, and CVD-safe palette suggestions. All computation runs locally in the browser; images are never uploaded to any server.
map.红色盲/绿色盲/蓝色盲采用 Machado、Oliveira 与 Fernand: Protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia use the linear RGB transformation matrices of Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes (2009), which merge the three steps "sRGB → LMS cone response → deficient-cone compensation → inverse" into a single 3×3 matrix acting on linear-light RGB. Anomaly types are obtained by linearly interpolating between the identity matrix and the full matrix by severity. Achromatopsia is grayscaled directly using Rec.709 luminance. Blue-cone monochromacy is treated as an approximate model: luminance follows the scotopic luminous-efficiency function V′(λ) (rods respond very weakly at the red end and most sensitively at the green end, so patients see red as darkest and green as brightest), and hue keeps only the S-cone "blue excess" relative to a same-luminance gray, hence white leans blue, yellow turns gray, and red turns dark gray. Color difference goes sRGB → CIE XYZ(D65) → CIE Lab, offering ΔE76 and ΔE2000 metrics.
map.严重度仅在色弱型（anomaly）上按默认 60% 起算；完全型（opia）默认: Severity starts at a default 60% for anomaly types only; full types (opia) default to 100%. Drag the slider to observe the continuous change from mild anomaly to full color blindness.

To confirm whether you have a color-vision deficiency, get a professional exam at a medical institution. Known model limitations: blue-cone monochromacy is an approximate implementation; severity interpolation uses a linear scheme and deviates from real anomaly spectral responses; different displays' gamut and brightness also affect the look.
